related_resources.reason: Books 18–24: the shield, Hector, funeral games, and Priam.
Achilles’ grief, return, and compassion for Priam.
Close commentary on the response to Hector’s death and burial.

work.note: 013000 opening places formation in something like the eighth or seventh century BCE and stresses debated oral composition/transcription. This date is not the legendary Trojan War; the Odyssey is not automatically assigned the Iliad’s date.
work.label: 8th–7th centuries BCE · debated formation

setting.label: c. 1200 BCE · conventional Trojan heroic frame
setting.note: Conventional Bronze Age frame for the Trojan War and its aftermath; this is a sorting anchor, not a claim that the war or marvelous voyages happened in this year. The poems mix periods. Their formation and surviving witnesses are separate. See discovery-homeric-setting and the 013000 opening; British Museum Troy exhibition notes that Homer’s war has not been established as a historical event.

creators.name: Homer
creators.note: Traditional attribution of a layered and transmitted text; not proof of a single historical author.

description: Tells of Achilles’ return, Hector’s death and Priam’s appeal for his son’s body, interpreting the shield, funeral rites and fragile recognition of shared grief at the epic’s close.
